articles.title: Slow and Steady: local, open-source AI that helps you work without urgency or cloud lock-in
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady Slow and Steady is a personal AI workspace that runs on the machine in front of you. The idea is sloth-shape…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Slow and Steady is a personal AI workspace that runs on the machine in front of you. The idea is sloth-shaped on purpose. Most “AI assistants” ask you to open an account, paste private text into someone else’s API, and keep paying per token. That is a lot of fuss for a tool that is supposed to take work off your plate. This app does the opposite: install it once, talk to an open-source model on localhost, and keep the conversation in a SQLite file on disk. It helps with the work people put off: explain a hard topic, tidy a paragraph, sketch a project, walk through a code snippet, or just sit with a calm chat window. The computer does the drafting. You stay in the chair.

articles.title: Make your v0 or Cursor app stop looking AI-built in 10 minutes
articles.excerpt: If you've built a landing page with v0, Cursor, Lovable or Bolt, you've probably had this moment: you put it next to someone else's and it's the same page. Purple-to-blue gradient, centred headline, o…
articles.body: If you've built a landing page with v0, Cursor, Lovable or Bolt, you've probably had this moment: you put it next to someone else's and it's the same page. Purple-to-blue gradient, centred headline, one font, three feature cards with an icon in a circle, a pricing table, and a "Get started" button that does nothing you can see. Nothing on that page is broken. It's the average of every landing page the model has seen, and that's what you get when you don't ask for anything specific. Visitors recognise it within seconds, though, and some of them decide the product behind it got the same amount of thought. Here are the five tells I look for and a fix for each. Every fix is a couple of minutes in a Next.js App Router project with Tailwind CSS v4.

articles.title: The Inverse of `.gitignore`: How Losing a `.env` Turned Into safekeep
articles.excerpt: The incident It started, as most of these things do, with a .env. I was mid-refactor, needed a key I was sure I'd written down, and the file wasn't gone. Deleted in a cleanup pass I did at 1am, along…
articles.body: The incident It started, as most of these things do, with a .env . I was mid-refactor, needed a key I was sure I'd written down, and the file wasn't there. Not "stale" — gone . Deleted in a cleanup pass I did at 1am, along with a .local.json and a couple of notes I'd been keeping next to the code. The saving grace was a manual backup — a tarball I'd thrown onto an external disk "just in case" maybe six months earlier. So the damage was two days of archaeology, not two weeks. But the feeling stuck: my source code had three remotes and a CI pipeline, and my secrets had… nothing. My own discipline. The problem: .gitignore protects the repo, not the file .gitignore is doing exactly the right job.

articles.title: Green Screen vs AI Background Removal: They're Not Playing the Same Game (Scenario Table Inside)
articles.excerpt: Whenever someone asks whether they should buy a green screen or just let AI cut the background out of their video, the thread turns into a turf war. It shouldn't, because the two options settle their…
articles.body: Whenever someone asks whether they should buy a green screen or just let AI cut the background out of their video, the thread turns into a turf war. It shouldn't, because the two options settle their costs at different moments. Chroma keying charges you up front — in setup, lighting, and floorspace — and then hands you a matte that stays put even when the footage turns nasty: flyaway hair, quick gestures, someone pacing across frame. An automatic cutout charges nothing at the door and then makes a fresh bet on every single frame, which looks like magic on well-separated footage and falls apart precisely when the going gets hard. Recurring content you can stage? Key it. Footage that already exists, came off a phone, or can't be reshot?

articles.title: Top 5 Ways to Humanize ChatGPT Responses in Your App (2026): System Prompts, Post-Processing and Tools
articles.excerpt: Updated October 2026. If you've shipped an LLM feature, you've probably had this feedback: "It works, but it sounds like a robot." Users notice the bullet-point reflex, the "Great question!" opener an…
articles.body: Updated October 2026. If you've shipped an LLM feature, you've probably had this feedback: "It works, but it sounds like a robot." Users notice the bullet-point reflex, the "Great question!" opener and the closing "Let me know if you have any other questions!" These patterns make a support bot feel scripted and a writing assistant feel generic. This is a practical list of fixes, from cheapest to most involved, for developers who want LLM responses that sound like their product rather than like a default assistant. First, define "human" for your product Nielsen Norman Group describes tone of voice along four dimensions: funny vs. serious, formal vs. casual, respectful vs. irreverent, and enthusiastic vs. matter-of-fact. Pick a point on each before you touch a prompt.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 20, 1970: The Soviet Union launches last-ever Zond moon mission
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. This was the last mission in the Zond program. After the first three Zond missions explored Venus and Mars , the next ones were circumlunar missions that flew around the moon before returning to Earth. Although there was no crew on board, the Zond spacecraft was designed with cosmonauts in mind. The Zond missions served as test flights for the Soviet Union's plans to send cosmonauts to the moon. But those plans for crewed flights never came to fruition. This was partly because the U.S. had already put astronauts on the moon , but also because the Zond missions had a lot of technical problems. Zond 8 was considered a success — even though its guidance system malfunctioned on the way back to Earth.

articles.body: Large language models are set to go lunar. A computer capable of running AI software is one of the payloads aboard Astrolab’s FLIP lunar rover, which is slated to head to Earth’s celestial companion as early as November 2026. The 480-kilogram FLIP rover, short for “FLEX Lunar Innovation Platform,” is the first in a series of vehicles NASA has contracted from Astrolab, including future buggies that will move Artemis astronauts across the moon’s surface. Fitted with deformable wheels engineered for the rugged terrain and designed to survive at least 150 hours of the frigid lunar night, FLIP will carry 20 scientific payloads , including a lidar 3D mapper and a sensor to measure concentrations of the isotope helium-3 in lunar regolith.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos is playing the long game with Blue Origin (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: If Blue Origin goes public, it will have to meet the expectations of shareholders. Jeff Bezos may therefore want to establish a stronger business before committing to a listing.
articles.body: Daniel Biedermann is a partner at NewSpace Capital. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . Jeff Bezos , the founder and former CEO of Amazon, recently said that Blue Origin , his space technology company, is likely to go public in the coming years. The announcement has (unsurprisingly) attracted considerable attention, not least because Bezos has spent more than two decades financing the company largely from his personal wealth. He has invested billions of dollars in developing rockets , spacecraft and other forms of technology, often with very little prospect of an immediate return. But although Bezos has now raised the possibility of an initial public offering, he has given no firm indication of when one might happen.
